mainTopic: Does רבי מאיר make דרבנן rules as strong as Torah law? רב ששת's objection, רב יוסף's answer, רבינא's challenge, אביי's and רבא's review, and a new משנה on items with no אונאה
overview: Before this amud, רבי אלעזר asked whether the חכמים made their own rules as strong as Torah law, and שמואל answered by quoting רבי מאיר. רב ששת objected. The amud opens with the end of his objection: for real מעשר שני, which is דאורייתא, silver may be redeemed onto copper only under pressure, yet for דמאי, which is only דרבנן, רבי מאיר allows it freely. רב יוסף answers that רבי מאיר is lenient only about redeeming דמאי. About eating it he is strict, as a ברייתא about selling דמאי shows. רבינא challenges this from a משנה where רבי מאיר lets someone tithe bread bought from a baker even across many molds. אביי then reviews the whole debate. רבי אלעזר's question was good, but שמואל's answer was weak. רב ששת's objection missed the point, but רב יוסף answered it well. רבינא's baker case proves nothing, because a baker buys from only one supplier. רבא disagrees and says שמואל's answer works, since 'death' is one category. Finally a new משנה lists slaves, documents, land and הקדש as items with no אונאה, no thief's extra payments, and special guardian rules. רבי שמעון's view continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Silver onto copper only under pressure
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes quoting a source: for real מעשר שני, one may redeem silver coins onto copper only under pressure, and must later switch back to silver.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because the חכמים said: one may redeem silver onto copper under pressure. He is not meant to leave it that way. He must later redeem the copper back onto silver.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing the quote of a source about redeeming real מעשר שני coins. It sets up the inference in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally מעשר שני money should stay as silver. Switching silver to copper is allowed only as an emergency step, and even then it must be switched back to silver later.

keyTerms.meaning: We redeem: move the holiness of מעשר שני onto something else
He goes back and redeems them again

phrases.english: Because they said:
phrases.notes: "They" means the חכמים. This is the end of a longer quote that started before this section.

phrases.english: One may redeem (it) silver onto copper, under pressure,
phrases.notes: Some versions don't have the word in round brackets; the meaning stays the same.

phrases.english: not that he should leave it that way,
but rather that he goes back and redeems them onto silver.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes a source quote begun before this section.
steps.raayaObject: That redeeming real מעשר שני silver onto copper is limited
steps.raayaSupportSource: A source about redeeming מעשר שני coins, quoted in the words of the חכמים

steps.title: Inference: only under pressure, not normally
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that the source says 'under pressure,' so without pressure it is not allowed. This shows that רבי מאיר is easier on דמאי than on real מעשר שני.
steps.simpleTranslation: At any rate, the source says one may redeem under pressure. Under pressure, yes. Not under pressure, no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws the key point from the source: silver onto copper is allowed only when there is pressure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For real מעשר שני, which is דאורייתא, this switch is an emergency step only. With דמאי, which is only דרבנן, רבי מאיר allowed it from the start. This completes רב ששת's objection to שמואל: רבי מאיר does not seem to make rabbinic rules as strong as Torah law.

keyTerms.meaning: At any rate, it teaches: the key point we take from the source

steps.whatToRemember: For real מעשר שני, silver onto copper is allowed only under pressure. רבי מאיר allows more for דמאי, so he is lenient about redeeming דמאי.

phrases.english: At any rate, it teaches: one redeems under pressure,
under pressure, yes;
not under pressure, no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the inference from the source quoted in step 1.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי מאיר is more lenient about redeeming דמאי than real מעשר שני
steps.raayaSupportSource: The word מִדּוֹחַק in the quoted source

steps.title: רב יוסף: lenient on redeeming, strict on eating
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף says that although רבי מאיר is lenient about redeeming דמאי, he is strict about eating it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: even though רבי מאיר is lenient about redeeming it, he is strict about eating it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף adds a limit to what we just learned about רבי מאיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We might think רבי מאיר is easygoing about דמאי in every way. רב יוסף splits it: redeeming is easy, but he is careful that nobody eats דמאי without tithing it.
steps.whyThisMatters: This split between redeeming and eating is what רבינא challenges in step 6.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁמֵּיקֵל רַבִּי מֵאִיר בְּפִדְיוֹנוֹ,
phrases.english: Even though Rabbi Meir is lenient about its redemption,
phrases.notes: "Its" means the מעשר שני of דמאי.

phrases.english: he is strict about its eating,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב ששת's objection (steps 1-2) by limiting רבי מאיר's leniency to redemption only.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי מאיר is lenient in redeeming דמאי but strict about eating it untithed.

steps.title: Proof: רבי מאיר makes a homeowner tithe
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף brings a ברייתא: only a סיטון may sell דמאי as is. A בעל הבית must tithe in any case, says רבי מאיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: they allowed only a wholesaler to sell דמאי. But a homeowner, either way, must tithe. These are the words of רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף proves his point with a ברייתא about who may sell דמאי without tithing it first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A סיטון buys from many people and sells in bulk, so he may sell without tithing. A בעל הבית must tithe before selling, whether he sells a lot or a little. This shows רבי מאיר worries that someone will end up eating untithed דמאי.

keyTerms.meaning: Produce bought from an עם הארץ that may not have been tithed

phrases.english: As it is taught: they permitted selling דמאי
only to a wholesaler alone.
But a homeowner:

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין כָּךְ וּבֵין כָּךְ, צָרִיךְ לְעַשֵּׂר,
phrases.english: whether this way or that way, must tithe,
phrases.notes: Either way means whether he sells in large amounts or in small amounts.

phrases.english: these are the words of Rabbi Meir.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב יוסף's claim in step 3.
steps.raayaObject: רבי מאיר is strict about eating דמאי

steps.title: The חכמים let anyone pass on דמאי
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: the חכמים say a סיטון and a בעל הבית may both sell, send, or give דמאי without worry.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the חכמים say: both the wholesaler and the homeowner may sell it, send it to a friend, or give it to him as a gift, and he need not worry.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives the other side, which shows by contrast how strict רבי מאיר is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים trust that the person receiving the דמאי will tithe it himself. רבי מאיר does not rely on that, which is exactly why רב יוסף calls him strict about eating.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי מאיר: a בעל הבית must tithe דמאי before passing it on. חכמים: anyone may pass it on, and the one who receives it tithes. So רבי מאיר is strict about eating דמאי.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis say:
both the wholesaler and the homeowner
may sell, and send to his friend,
and give to him as a gift, and need not worry.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא begun in step 4 and shows the contrast.
steps.raayaObject: רבי מאיר is strict about eating דמאי, compared to the חכמים
steps.raayaSupportSource: The second half of the same ברייתא

steps.title: רבינא challenges from bread bought from a baker
steps.stepSummary: רבינא quotes a משנה where רבי מאיר lets someone who bought from a baker tithe warm bread for cold, cold for warm, and even across many molds.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא objected: one who buys from a baker may tithe from the warm bread for the cold, and from the cold for the warm, and even from loaves of many molds. These are the words of רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא begins a challenge to רב יוסף by quoting a משנה. This step sets up the attack, and steps 7 and 8 spell out exactly where the problem lies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here רבי מאיר seems relaxed about how bread bought from an untrustworthy baker gets tithed. That seems to clash with רב יוסף's claim that רבי מאיר is strict about eating דמאי.

phrases.english: Ravina raised an objection:
One who buys from a baker,
may tithe from the warm for the cold,
and from the cold for the warm,
and even from many molds,
these are the words of Rabbi Meir.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב יוסף's claim from step 3 using a different source.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's claim that רבי מאיר is strict about eating דמאי
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משנה shows רבי מאיר being relaxed about how bread from an untrustworthy baker is tithed, which seems to clash with being strict about eating דמאי. Steps 7 and 8 show that the real problem is the 'many molds' ruling.

steps.title: Cold bread for warm bread is understandable
steps.stepSummary: רבינא grants that taking מעשר from cold bread for warm bread makes sense, based on רבי אילעאי's teaching that תרומה taken from worse produce for better produce still counts.
steps.simpleTranslation: Granted, taking from cold bread for warm bread is fine, like רבי אילעאי taught. He learned from the פסוק 'you shall bear no sin… when you set apart the best of it' that if someone takes תרומה from bad produce for good produce, it still counts as תרומה. If it didn't count, why would there be any 'sin'?
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא is setting up his challenge. First he admits which part of the משנה is not a problem, and then (in the next step) he will show which part is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Cold bread is lower quality than warm bread. Doing this is not ideal, but רבי אילעאי shows from the פסוק that bad-for-good תרומה still works, since the Torah calls it a 'sin', and you only sin if you actually did something real. So this part of רבי מאיר's ruling can be explained without saying he is lenient about דמאי.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Granted' or 'it makes sense'. It opens the part of a challenge that is not a problem, before the 'but' comes.
The portion of produce set aside and given to a כהן.
Taking from the worse-quality produce to cover the better-quality produce.
'Bearing sin', meaning being guilty of doing something wrong.

phrases.english: Granted, taking from the cold bread for the warm bread,
phrases.notes: This goes back to the משנה quoted in step 6 about bread bought from a baker.

phrases.english: that fits with רבי אילעאי's teaching.
For רבי אילעאי said:

phrases.aramaic: מִנַּיִן לַתּוֹרֵם מִן הָרָעָה עַל הַיָּפָה
phrases.english: From where do we know that one who separates תרומה from poor produce for good produce
that his תרומה counts as תרומה?
As it says: "And you shall bear no sin because of it
when you set apart the best of it from it."

phrases.aramaic: אִם אֵינוֹ קֹדֶשׁ, נְשִׂיאַת חֵטְא לָמָּה?
phrases.english: If it does not become holy, why would there be bearing of sin?

phrases.aramaic: מִכָּאן לַתּוֹרֵם מִן הָרָעָה עַל הַיָּפָה,
phrases.english: From here we learn that one who separates from poor produce for good produce,
his תרומה counts as תרומה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רבינא's challenge from step 6 by first explaining the part of the משנה that causes no difficulty.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's claim (step 3) that רבי מאיר is strict about eating דמאי.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: This is the 'granted' half. It sets aside the cold-for-warm case so the real problem (many molds) stands out.
steps.raayaObject: That cold-for-warm tithing is valid even without any leniency about דמאי.

steps.title: But many different molds is a real problem
steps.stepSummary: רבינא's real difficulty: allowing מעשר across many molds risks taking from untithed loaves for tithed ones, or the reverse. So רבי מאיר seems lenient about eating דמאי.
steps.simpleTranslation: But allowing it even from many different molds is a problem! We should worry that he will end up taking from loaves that still need tithing for loaves that are already exempt, or from exempt loaves for ones that need tithing!
steps.whatsHappening: This is the main punch of רבינא's question. The many-molds ruling seems to ignore a real risk, which suggests רבי מאיר is easygoing about eating דמאי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Loaves from different molds may have come from different sources, so some might already be tithed and some not. Tithing from one batch for another could fail. Since רבי מאיר allows it anyway, he seems lenient about eating דמאי, which goes against רב יוסף's claim in step 3.

keyTerms.meaning: Molds or shapes that the bread is baked in.
'Let us be concerned', meaning there should be a worry here.
Produce that still must be tithed.
Produce that is exempt, because it was already tithed.

phrases.english: But even from many molds,
let us worry that perhaps he will come to separate
from the obligated loaves for the exempt ones,
phrases.notes: 'Obligated' means loaves that still need tithing, and 'exempt' means loaves already tithed.

phrases.english: or from the exempt loaves for the obligated ones!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The 'but' that follows the 'granted' of step 7. It names the part of the משנה that really is difficult.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's statement that רבי מאיר is strict about eating דמאי.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If רבי מאיר were strict about eating דמאי, he would worry about mixing tithed and untithed loaves. Allowing many molds shows he is lenient.

steps.title: אביי: שמואל's answer to רבי אלעזר was weak
steps.stepSummary: אביי says רבי אלעזר's question was a good one, but שמואל's answer does not work. רבי אלעזר asked about a sin punished by death from Heaven, while שמואל answered from a case of death by בית דין, which may be more serious.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: רבי אלעזר asked a good question, but שמואל did not answer it well. רבי אלעזר was asking about something punished by death from Heaven, and שמואל answered from something punished by death by בית דין. Maybe death by בית דין is different because it is more severe!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the start of the debate, and אביי grades each answer. Here he rejects שמואל's answer to רבי אלעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר's case carried death from Heaven. שמואל proved from רבי מאיר in a case carrying death by בית דין that חכמים made their rules as strong as Torah law. אביי says the proof doesn't carry over. Maybe רבי מאיר is strict only in the more severe category, so the question still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Death from Heaven, a punishment from ה׳ and not from a court.
Death carried out by the court.

phrases.english: אביי said:

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר שַׁפִּיר קָא קַשְׁיָא לֵיהּ,
phrases.english: רבי אלעזר asked a good question,

phrases.aramaic: וּשְׁמוּאֵל לָא שַׁפִּיר קָא מְשַׁנֵּי לֵיהּ.
phrases.english: and שמואל did not answer him well.
For what troubled רבי אלעזר
was a case of death from Heaven,

phrases.aramaic: וּמְשַׁנֵּי לֵיהּ שְׁמוּאֵל: מִיתַת בֵּית דִּין.
phrases.english: and שמואל answered him from a case of death by בית דין.

phrases.aramaic: דִּלְמָא שָׁאנֵי מִיתַת בֵּית דִּין דַּחֲמִירָא!
phrases.english: Perhaps death by בית דין is different, since it is more severe!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר שַׁפִּיר קָא קַשְׁיָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves רבינא's challenge and goes back to the opening exchange between רבי אלעזר and שמואל to evaluate it.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects שמואל's proof, so in אביי's view רבי אלעזר's question still stands. In step 13, רבא disagrees and defends שמואל.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof comes from a more severe category (death by בית דין) and is applied to a lighter one (death from Heaven).

steps.title: אביי: רב ששת's objection was weak, but רב יוסף answered it well
steps.stepSummary: אביי says רב ששת's objection did not fit, because רבי אלעזר and שמואל were talking about death penalties while רב ששת brought a plain לאו. Still, on רב ששת's own terms, רב יוסף's answer was correct.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב ששת did not object well. They (רבי אלעזר and שמואל) were talking about death penalties, and רב ששת objected from a plain לאו, as it says 'You may not eat within your gates.' But as far as רב ששת's objection goes, רב יוסף answered it well.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי finishes grading the debate. He says רב ששת's challenge missed the point, but רב יוסף's answer to it was right.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב ששת's proof came from מעשר שני, which is only a לאו and not a death penalty, so it can't really challenge a discussion about death penalties. Even so, the point רב יוסף made still holds within that objection: רבי מאיר is lenient about redeeming דמאי but strict about eating it.

keyTerms.meaning: A plain Torah prohibition, without a death penalty.
'Within your gates', meaning outside ירושלים, where מעשר שני may not be eaten.

steps.whatToRemember: אביי's grades: רבי אלעזר's question was good. שמואל's answer was weak, because death by בית דין is more severe. רב ששת's objection was weak, because a plain לאו can't be compared to a death penalty. רב יוסף's answer to רב ששת was correct.

phrases.aramaic: וְרַב שֵׁשֶׁת לָא שַׁפִּיר קָא מוֹתֵיב לֵיהּ,
phrases.english: And רב ששת did not object to him well,
for they are talking about death penalties.
and רב ששת objects from a plain prohibition,
as it is written: "You may not eat within your gates."
But as for the objection רב ששת raised,

phrases.aramaic: רַב יוֹסֵף שַׁפִּיר קָא מְשַׁנֵּי לֵיהּ.
phrases.english: רב יוסף answered him well.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַב שֵׁשֶׁת לָא שַׁפִּיר קָא מוֹתֵיב לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues אביי's review from step 9, moving from שמואל's answer to רב ששת's objection and רב יוסף's reply.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects רב ששת's objection as not relevant to the death-penalty discussion.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It compares a plain לאו (eating מעשר שני outside ירושלים) to cases with a death penalty.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רב ששת's challenge doesn't really fit the original question. Within that challenge, though, רב יוסף was right that רבי מאיר is lenient on redeeming דמאי but strict on eating it.

steps.title: Why did רבינא not use the bread-merchant case?
steps.stepSummary: אביי continues his review: instead of objecting to רב יוסף from the baker case, רבינא could have found support for רב יוסף in the bread-merchant (פלטר) case, where רבי מאיר requires tithing from each mold separately.
steps.simpleTranslation: But as for רבינא: instead of raising an objection from the baker, he should have brought support from the bread merchant! For we learned: one who buys from a bread merchant tithes from each and every mold. These are the words of רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי now judges רבינא's objection. He points to a משנה where רבי מאיר is strict, which would actually support רב יוסף, and so sets up the next step's point that the baker case proves nothing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the baker case (steps 6-8), רבי מאיר allowed tithing across many molds, and that looked lenient about eating דמאי. In the merchant case he requires each mold to be tithed by itself, which looks strict and backs רב יוסף. So the two cases point in opposite directions, and רבינא's choice of the baker case seems one-sided.

keyTerms.meaning: A bread merchant or dealer who sells bread he gets from others
A baker who bakes his own bread
A mold or bread pan. Loaves from the same mold usually come from the same batch
To support, to bring backing for a view

phrases.english: But as for רבינא,
rather than raising an objection from the baker,
phrases.notes: This is the baker משנה רבינא quoted back in step 6.

phrases.english: let him bring support from the bread merchant!
For we learned: One who buys from a bread merchant
tithes from each and every mold separately,
these are the words of רבי מאיר.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא רָבִינָא, עַד דְּמוֹתֵיב מִנַּחְתּוֹם לְסַיַּיע לֵיהּ מִפַּלְטֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to רבינא's difficulty (steps 6-8) and questions which source he chose.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A parallel משנה about a bread merchant shows רבי מאיר being strict about tithing across molds, which supports רב יוסף. So the baker case alone cannot refute רב יוסף.

steps.title: The merchant case does not apply, and neither does the baker case
steps.stepSummary: The merchant case is different because a merchant buys from two or three suppliers. But then the baker case is no proof either, because a baker buys his grain from only one person.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, what must you say? A merchant buys from two or three people. Then a baker too: he buys from one person.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי explains why the merchant case says nothing on this topic. Then he uses the same reasoning to take apart רבינא's baker case too, finishing his verdict that רבינא's objection was not a good one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר is strict with a merchant only because the bread comes from several suppliers, and one may have tithed while another did not. A baker gets all his grain from one supplier, so all the loaves have the same status, and tithing across molds carries no risk. So רבי מאיר's leniency with the baker is not leniency about דמאי at all, and רבינא's difficulty falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, what must you say? This opens the only answer that works
A person, a man (here, a supplier)

steps.confusionAlert: Step 12 does not prove that רבי מאיר is lenient or strict about דמאי. It shows that neither bread case tells us anything, because in each one the ruling depends on how many suppliers there are.

phrases.english: Rather, what must you say?
A merchant buys from two or three people,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 11, and then turns that answer against רבינא's own source.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: רבינא's difficulty from the baker case (step 8)
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A baker buys from one supplier, so there is no real risk of mixing tithed and untithed loaves. רבי מאיר's ruling therefore shows no leniency about דמאי.

steps.title: רבא defends שמואל: death is one category
steps.stepSummary: רבא disagrees with אביי and says שמואל's answer to רבי אלעזר was good, because death by בית דין and death by Heaven are both part of one category of 'death'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: שמואל answered him well, because 'death' is one category in the world.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers אביי's rejection from step 9. He says שמואל was right to answer a question about death by Heaven with a case of death by בית דין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי claimed (step 9) that the two kinds of death are too different to compare, since death by בית דין may be more serious. רבא says both fall under one heading, 'death'. So a proof from one kind of death works for the other, and שמואל's answer stands.

keyTerms.meaning: He answers well, the answer is a good one
Death by the hand of Heaven

steps.whatToRemember: אביי split death by בית דין from death by Heaven. רבא joins them into one category of 'death', so שמואל's proof works.

phrases.english: רבא said:
שמואל answers him well,
phrases.notes: 'Him' is רבי אלעזר, whose question שמואל answered back in the earlier discussion.

phrases.english: for there is one category of 'death' in the world.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר: שְׁמוּאֵל שַׁפִּיר קָא מְשַׁנֵּי לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to אביי's rejection of שמואל in step 9 and disagrees with it.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Unifying categories: both kinds of death count as one category
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Death by בית דין is too different from death by Heaven to compare (אביי)
steps.terutzMaskana: Both are 'death', so שמואל's proof works
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: According to רבא, שמואל's answer to רבי אלעזר stands.

steps.title: New משנה: items with no אונאה, no double payment, and special guardian rules
steps.stepSummary: The משנה lists four kinds of items: slaves, documents, land, and הקדש. They are not subject to אונאה, to כפל, or to four-and-five payment. An unpaid guardian of them does not swear, and a paid guardian does not pay. Then רבי שמעון begins to give his view.
steps.simpleTranslation: These are items that have no אונאה: slaves, documents, land, and consecrated property. They have no double payment and no four-and-five payment. An unpaid guardian does not take an oath, and a paid guardian does not pay. רבי שמעון says:
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins, still in the same chapter. It lists items that are left out of several monetary laws. רבי שמעון's opinion starts at the end and continues in the next part.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These items still belong to the world of buying, selling, theft, and guarding. The משנה is pointing out exceptions where certain Torah rules do not apply to them. The same list of four is excluded from overcharging (אונאה), from the thief's extra payments, and from the usual duties of guardians.

keyTerms.meaning: Overcharging or underpaying in a sale (by one-sixth or more)
Property consecrated to the בית המקדש
Four or five times the value, paid when a thief slaughters or sells a stolen sheep or ox

steps.confusionAlert: The משנה does not say these items cannot be sold, stolen, or guarded. It only says certain special rules (אונאה, extra payments, guardian oaths and payments) do not apply to them.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: Slaves, documents, land, and הקדש are left out of אונאה, double payment, four-and-five payment, the unpaid guardian's oath, and the paid guardian's payment.
